question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(1-x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{1-(1-x)^{2}}\cdot (1-x)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-(1-2x+{x}^{2})}\cdot (-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2x-{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-2x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x(x-2)}.\end{aligned}
$$
